answer: Continuous physical-labor attestation requires each identity to sustain a verifiable thread of logged field work—sensor-stamped, location-bound tasks like timber hauling or tundra soil sampling—validated by peers who share the same work history. Registration alone grants nothing; the identity only becomes usable as the work log accumulates, and tasks are assigned through non-transferable labor slots. To run N sybils, an attacker must physically perform N parallel work tracks, paying in real hours, travel, and supervision, since logs cannot be copied or delegated.
